root_cause: The _keydown handler in tab.js does not skip disabled tabs when determining the next active element, causing ArrowRight to attempt focus on a disabled button. Since disabled buttons cannot receive focus, focus remains unchanged and the disabled tab incorrectly receives aria-selected=true.
repair_strategy: Modify the _keydown method to iterate over candidate next elements returned by getNextActiveElement, skipping any that are disabled via isDisabled, with a loop guard to prevent infinite cycling when all tabs are disabled.
expected_accessibility_effect: ArrowRight will now move focus to the next enabled tab (Billing) and set aria-selected=true on that tab, complying with keyboard navigation that skips disabled controls.
functional_risks: Infinite loop guard prevents hanging if all tabs are disabled.
Change assumes disabling a tab means it should be skipped in arrow navigation; if other code relied on selecting disabled tabs via arrows, that behavior will change.
Ensure that tab activation logic still works correctly for enabled tabs after the skip logic.
verification_requirements: Verify that ArrowRight from Account moves focus to Billing and sets aria-selected=true on Billing.
Verify that ArrowLeft from Billing wraps to Account (skipping disabled Notifications).
Confirm that focus does not land on the disabled Notifications tab when using arrow keys.
Ensure that pressing Tab still navigates into tabpanels as expected.
Check that the disabled tab retains its disabled attribute and is not focusable.
